title: Read a scene before trying to translate it
steps: Find a single scene boundary and its register (horizontal tier).
Identify the king, the deity facing him, and the action or offered object.
Separate royal names above the king, the action label between figures, and divine names/speeches near the gods.
Check neighbouring scenes for a relationship; do not assume an entire wall is one chronological story.

claims.text: Royal identity, ritual action labels and divine speech occupy distinguishable parts of the scene.

citations.locator: Structure of Ritual Scenes: paragraphs on upper texts, label text and divine speeches

claims.text: The king normally faces inward and deities outward in the project’s description; this is scene composition, not a universal text-reading rule.

citations.locator: Structure of Ritual Scenes: opening paragraph

claims.text: Scenes occupy registers; individual scenes can be complete ritual acts, although small groups can form connected sequences.

limits: General visual literacy lesson, not a translation of any specific inscription.
A sign-direction and phonetic-reading exercise needs a verified panel, facsimile and edition.
